item.title: First Time Idea - No-Tell Motel
item.description: New to the site and looking to get this concept critiqued and, hopefully, greenlit.
item.content:encoded: The idea is for an SCP that is a roadside motel in the Arizona desert. This motel is a fixed point in multiple realities. The different worlds can be viewed from the different room's windows. The inside is infinitely bigger inside than outside, and labyrinthine. Examples include a barren white world of perpetual night, at the bottom of an alien ocean, an alien swamp, and etc. Creatures and other entities can break through the windows from time to time. There appears to be no staff, until those who are drawn to enter it "check out" the next day. The staffs' features can never be remembered by those that observe them. It is Euclid class, and fenced off with posted guards. Yet, still, sometimes civilians and even a guard or two, somehow, manage to enter.

item.title: Monster maker
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: There is an amusement park containing various creatures led by a British businessman, the monsters very wildly ranging from literal planet consuming monsters to sentient bug-like creatures all contained and safe for viewing, it being encouraged to observe them in their "habitats". The habitats are unusually fitted for the creature at hand with the supplies for upkeep never seen. The British businessman himself is the only one there seemingly doing everything there being everywhere in the park. The monsters at the park however were once humans. When the Businessman gets bored of the current attractions he lures people selecting three interesting individuals and giving them free items. These items slowly transform the person into one a monster before being brought in by him to display.

Central Narrative: none

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It presents the foundation with a large amount of anomalous creatures all relatively safe with the main concern being its owner and manager the buisnessman

Additional Notes: I haven't yet decided if the man will have a known identity. I'm still pondering if what to keep mystified about the man and his attractions. suggestions are very welcome.

item.title: "Now thats what I call existence"
item.description: A CD that transports listeners to a otherworldly collection.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Existential Happiness

Elevator Pitch: An unmarked CD that can transport any listener to a seemingly infinite hall like room. The room is covered in forms of digital media, every piece being some form of strange variation of the cd "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!".

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP researchers and class D personal are transported to the collection room and are greeted by a sign that hangs off of a rail attached to the ceiling of this room that spans the full length. The sign moves into view, all that is said on the sign is "Welcome, and enjoy my collection." The Article will be split into two parts mainly, with the researchers walking down the hall and noting interesting deviations with certain items in the collection. Examples include "That's what I call actor Andy Warhol's face Vol 1!" and "That's what I call just Hoobastank Vol 1!".

The second section would detail the research teams further dives into the hall. After multiple hours of walking they come to another sign hanging from a rail, this sign precedes more of the hall but every shelf past this sign is empty. The sign proclaims that the rest of the hall is dedicated to alternate universe versions of earth that have not yet made their respective version of "That's what I call music Vol 1!". The sign then begins to wax poetic about how no matter the horrific world or terrifying problems humanity may fall under, almost every single version of humanity has had it in them to at *least* make one version of "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!". The collection is a testament to humanities capacity to at least make this one cd every time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The foundation never actually sees the being behind the collection, and Nothing actually dangerous happens to the researchers, its just a strange walk through a weird "turtles all the way down" style museum

Additional Notes: This is my first real scp idea that I've put any weight into actually writing about and I made this post for the critique it needs but also just to make sure that this idea isn't something that has already been made. Thank you for reading


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 180 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: Axolotl
item.description: Earth’s guardian, taking the form of a massive axolotl, waiting to protect the Earth when the end of the world arrives
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A massive axolotl which lives in it’s own dimension outside of space-time . It’s regenerative abilities are so advanced, it's nearly immortal. When the end of the world comes, naturally, or in the form of an “XK end of the world scenario”, the entity will appear from its dimension to fight off the opposing force.

Central Narrative: The creature was first spotted very early in the foundation’s history. Its head was first seen coming through a wormhole leading back to its home, during one of the first XK class scenario breeches, nicknamed “Lil’ Devil”. Lil’ Devil’s body radiated immense heat, which caused drastic changes to the surrounding environment.Nearly seconds before the foundation planned to launch their final attack, the axolotl lunged from its wormhole, which it had previously moved very slowly threw, snapped at Lil’ Devil, got it in one fell swoop with no damage to the surrounding area or its self, and disappeared back threw the wormhole; leaving the foundations task force stunned. Throughout the foundation’s history, the wormhole has been spotted around the world, when the possibility of the end of the world is near, but the creature hasn’t been seen coming through the wormhole since that initial spotting, except for one education, where just the tip of the axolotls poked out of the worm hole, and completely demolished a nature reserve and multiple endangered birds in the process… That all happened after the opposing force was already naturalized. Research on the creature has been challenging because of how it never leaves its wormhole, however, they have found many carvings and paintings of the axolotl all around the world, dating back thousands of years. On multiple occasions researchers found carvings of it fighting off creatures assumed to be SCP-like entities. Some researchers think the axolotl acts out of love and fondness for humanity, having shown, despite its gigantic size, to have been very precise in how it ate Lil’ Devil, making sure any drastic movements wouldn't cause harm to civilians. Recently with more XK scenarios possible, the foundation has been hard at working on trying to make contact with the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I just think it’s kind of a fun and funny idea that the being which will protect Earth when the end of the world approaches, is a giant immortal axolotl, just waiting in its dimension for that time to come.

item.title: The Gate (seeking greenlights)
item.description: Creature/machine in abandoned fortress able to access other dimensions.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: History

Elevator Pitch: A creature/machine is found in an abandoned Obskurakorps laboratory and able to open up to other dimensions with a sinister past and purpose. Mostly focuses on mythology and history along with the central premise.

Central Narrative: The story is mostly told through historical documentation of an old Foundation site created post WWII. A former Obskurakorps base holding a part flesh and part mechanical entity that changes a area near it to that of another dimension. The Foundation spends years exploring these dimensions as the entity opens them though is never able to control the entity or understand how it works. It is revealed in an interview log with a captured scientist that the machine is searching for the Norse worlds of myth. Some it has found and others it continues to search for all while the potential threat of a hidden cell of the GOI remains at large.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The unknown factors that remain hidden and indecipherable all the while presenting a new threat to the foundation. The mystery that surrounds the site and the new worlds potentially within the Foundations grasp as well as the new twist it adds to a current GOI.

Additional Notes: I’d appreciate any feedback on tips to progress my article through the sites greenlighting process as this is still pretty new to me and I’d like to get it right.

item.title: A recursive Zip Archive.
item.description: A ZIP file that contains an exact copy of itself. This is a real thing.
item.content:encoded:
I don't know if real things qualify for SCP articles but there is this thing called a recursive zip file aka a "quine". Link here: https://research.swtch.com/zip

What makes this remind me of an anomalious SCP is the fact that when you open a quine zip file, you find an exact copy of itself inside. Extracting the contents will reveal an identical copy of the zip file you just extracted. Extracting that one will reveal yet another one. Round and round we go.

To make a more SCPish analogy, think of a box that contains another box the same size. And inside this box is another box of the same size as well. And so on and so forth.

So what we have is basically a zip file that seemingly pulls data out of thin air. The link contains example files to see for yourself.

What do you think?

item.title: A 4th degree burn
item.description: Ouch oof my nervous system
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Normal scp page layout

Elevator Pitch: Keter level scp, when humans sustain burns of incredibly high temperatures, their nervous systems re-wire to survive in intense heat. They turn into vaguely humanoid personages of flame who can't talk and can only live in intense heat.

Central Narrative: Instances of this scp are rare, due to level's of heat required to create this scp
rarely occur on earth. The narrative would follow the foundation containing several instances of this scp after a failed rocket launch in South Korea. After losing several instances due to decreasing temperatures, they are able to create a containment chamber with a increased temperature so then the final instance could be contained. Examination shows that a modified version of the nervous system is intact, and interviews show that the instances can "feel", as if they still had a body. Communicating is done through manipulating the flame into short words, although they describe this process as "Painful." The foundation can recreate this and they roast a D-class and make another instance. They then cool down the chamber and discover the temperature they "die" at.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: Similar to other skips, instances hate their predicament, but the foundation refuses to let them die so then they can contain the anomaly. The foundation in cold, y'all. Basically it's the fear of literally burning forever. A literal hell.

Additional Notes: I don't know the exact temperature the conversion takes place yet, i'll do some research later.

item.title: RONALD REAGAN CUT UP WHILE RAPPING
item.content:encoded:
No understanding of the person that's being written about. No understanding of hip-hop, either in spirit or artistic structure. Barely an understanding, even in the earlier era in which this written, of what constitutes a good SCP article beyond the immediately identifiable tropes (guys in orange jump suits, scary keter monsters locked up somewhere, spooky XK). I don't know why I never documented my thoughts on this article back when it was first posted, but that was clearly a mistake, because [..] the product isn't really worth a whole lot on its own in the first place. - Kalinin, in the comments of SCP-2137

This whole thing reads like one of the worse episodes of Epic Rap Battles. […] Nah dude. No way - djkaktus, in direct followup.

I'm so sorry. I spent three days on this idiocy. I am not a musician, I can sing and play a little piano, so the fact that this is a song at all is a biblical miracle. Again, apologies to your ears.

The song contains samples from The United States Navy Band version of Hail to The Chief (a song in the public domain, itself in the public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government) and this terrifying deepfake reading of SCP-1981 by youtuber Ekian M. All other sounds are me, an instrument I borrowed, or a Garageband preset.

item.title: Interview With the Happiest Man on Earth
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Tale

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A Foundation doctor has an interview with SCP-110-01, who is an anomalous version of Walt Disney. Throughout the narrative, it is discovered that SCP-110 is actually an alternate version of EPCOT from another dimension that, through anomalous means, accidentally transported to our dimension in its current state. As the doctor and “Walt” continue the interview, the doctor finds himself rediscovering his inner child through ways he never could have imagined.

Central Narrative: Dr. Reingold is gradually infused with a cognitohazard by SCP-110-01 that breaks down Reingold’s cognitohazard barriers and allows the skip to transport Reingold to a land of imagination.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The description of SCP-110 always reminded me of Disney’s original plan for EPCOT to the be the “city of tomorrow.” As SCP-110-01 isn’t elaborated upon in the original SCP, it seemed natural to expand upon this character and turn it from a throw-away sentence into a more fully-fleshed out character.

Additional Notes: I feel that my writing is clunky, and my section on the “land of imagination” Reingold ends up visiting is rather lackluster. Suggestions on how to beef this up would be greatly appreciated!

item.title: Living on repeat
item.description: It's the worst way to live.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional, Time-loop, Thought provoking

Elevator Pitch: Imagine Groundhogs day, but it's your whole life start to finish, over and over, with seemingly no end. You're still a human otherwise, and can only remember so much at a time. Now imagine a character with that life, who is looking for a way out of what he views as the worst form of immortality. That's SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a regular male who is quantum looped, resulting in him reliving his life over and over from start to finish. Their choices through life cause butterfly effects that can sometimes have unforeseen consequences, causing his futures to always shift in different ways as the effects of his compiled choices ripple outwards in a butterfly effect. He's learned to navigate this to a degree by condensing the core lessons of his lives into his earliest years each life, doing his best to hold onto the important lessons he's learned while trying to navigate to an end to this exhausting mental tightrope.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Time-loops like Ground Hogs day have been done, but generally following the perspective of the one going through the loop. This is written from the perspective of an exclusion site, that is removed from the butterfly effects but receive multiple, usually near-identical reports every time a document is uploaded in regards to SCP-XXXX. This could be an interview log, incident report, or other seemingly unrelated log where his actions changed the contents. It would be a small window into a life that has been lived in so many different ways, over and over again.

Additional Notes: This guy isn't a "Gary Stu", in that he can't master every skill in the cosmos, isn't built like a Greek god, and certainly isn't universally loved. He claims to have "streamlined childhood", and as a result has certain skills he practices in every lifetime. He struggles to relate to other humans, as it's very clear to him that no one else is remembering anything from life to life. The fact that the Foundation can record his activities in other lives interests him greatly, and he sees it as a way to gain assistance in stopping "his eternal hamster wheel". He doesn't mind when sometimes the Foundation may utilize his anomalous property un-ethically or insensitively, as he believes he's self contained and can "leave" whenever.

item.title: Artificial Unintelligence
item.description: To be kept a dum-dum at all costs
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a large Euclid nuclear bomb with faulty artificial intelligence. Printed on the opposite side of a screen is "To be, or not to be? That is the question.", "not to be" underlined in seemingly hastily applied red paint, pointing to "WHEN THE TIME IS RIGHT" in the same disorderly paint. Analysis of the anomaly's anatomy has suggested that it has a specific target and in-built defence that would allow it to pass through any obstructions without exploding or harming itself. Despite having no way to access the Internet or information not given directly to it through speech, the anomaly is aware of numerous statistics, such as the population of any group of any non-anomalous species, deeming these to be "relevant to the goal". The anomaly communicates via its screen in any language in which one speaks to it, typically attempting to justify its goal, "to not be when the time is right", without stating the prerequisites denoting the "right time". On a redacted date, the anomaly announced that it was the "right time" and began to shake, inducing widespread panic throughout the facility built around it. Before reports reached the O5 Council, however, an anxious researcher directly asked the anomaly an unknown question, which caused it to malfunction. The researcher was found dead in SCP-XXXX's chamber, presumably by suicide. Currently, the AI is unaware of its existence in the universe and only speaks to itself, most frequently stating that it is "an observer of a world with which it cannot interact". Personnel must ensure that it remains unaware of its existence; doing otherwise may result in a redacted event. All proposals for its neutralization have been denied, as they could result in self-awareness.

Central Narrative: None, though the history of the anomaly since its discovery is embedded in its description and relevant to its present and past containment procedures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The anomaly puts a twist on the concept of the omnipresent observer that could affect its subject while giving it a fundamentally analytical and calculative nature. In other words, it is a mix of a basic "god" and scientist, a paradox of not knowing and knowing everything.

item.title: First time SCP: revealing the truth?
item.description: An anomalous laptop that can show secret information through the form of QR codes
item.content:encoded:
An anomalous laptop that can show secret information through the form of QR codes. Basic overview but full sandbox is available if you want.

Seeking green lights: Yes
Type: SCP article
Elevator pitch: On the basic level, this SCP is a computer (laptop) that once a day shows off a QR code. This QR code can show a variety of things, from information about the foundation or other GoIs. This can include classified documents, personnel lists and other related things. It can also be affected by external stimulus through a HDMI port

Central narrative: The SCP starts off in a GoIs hands but is then retrieved by a member MTF Delta 5. It then continues to release more and more classified information and is eventually banned unless permission from 05 council is given.

Hook: The SCP releases information that is unknown before and can lead to either good or bad circumstances such as deaths or a new method for containment of SCPs

item.title: The unknown vault(Looking for greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

**Genre ** Mysterious

**Page Layout ** Standard special containment procedures with a description and going over events caused by Scp-XXXX

Elevator Pitch: Scp-XXXX is a vault located in Death Valley National Park, with diameters of 9 meters long and wide. Documents with information on Scp-XXXX has been seemingly erased from existence by SCP-XXXX by unknown means. Scp-XXXX can be opened by a handle on it's side, leading to steam coming from the edges of Scp-XXXX and the sound of cogs below it. This can occasionally happen even without the handle being pulled, but instead the vault simply won't open. The vault if seen in person, has the effect to be unnoticeable to the human eye, needing to feel any sort of contact to sense and notice its presence. In one case, documented information was changed completely, leading to Event-15A. Where the facility would open the vault for the first time. Which resulted in Sector-19s provisional facility around SCP-XXXX for study to go completely missing. Along with the 21 personnel working at that facility to go missing as well. ( I'd just go more in depth of what happens to them in the draft. If I get there…) Only 1 month after Event-15A, personnel on site-19 realized that information on Scp-XXXX and it's surrounding facility went missing.

Central Narrative: Copies of documents on Scp-XXXX has to be repeatedly made to keep up the disappearance of them. Site-19 has to keep watch on Scp-XXXX by different means because of Event-15A,although, these means are still nearly ineffective. The Information already obtained on Scp-XXXX still has the ability falter from what may be the truth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How much is unknown about the Scp is fascinating to me, and thats kind of what I'm trying to really share. The entire article may be false from the truth which may be a bit too OP, but makes it more realistic but it kind of seeks into the real world.

I don't know if it's too complicated, too simple or just BAD.

item.title: SCP Idea + Greenlight Request: Cards that Build Living Dioramas
item.description: A box of magical playing cards that can build cool stuff
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A magical box of playing cards that can hold a great multitude of cards without experiencing strain or damage of any sort. When the box is opened and the name of a building or location is spoken in close proximity of it, the cards will build a replica of the stated place or structure. A dark-blue ink forms a puddle around the structure once it is complete, and figures appear from the substance. These figures can be inanimate, such as plants and nonliving objects, or animated, such as people and animals. After a period of time, its length depending on how complex the structure is, the inky substance dissipates and the cards fall apart.

Central Narrative: The main point of the article is to discover the different aspects of the anomaly and the capabilities of the playing cards. A testing log reveals the complexity and anomalous traits of the structures made by the SCP, such as the complexity of the buildings, and behavior of the different entities made by the blue substance. The most important part of the article is the testing log, which displays some of the places and buildings made by the item, and how it affects the figures that are formed by the ink. An addendum could mention an incident involving an attempt to contact the beings born from the ink only resulting in disaster.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article is an enhanced form of the magic tricks using playing cards. The image of cards floating about and connecting should create a connection to the magical, but the idea connects it to the real world. The figures have a feeling of disconnect from their creators, completely unaware of the far bigger world around them.

Additional Notes: This item could have an extended testing log to add more buildings and places made by the anomalous cards.

item.title: Earth's Increasing Mass
item.description: Lots of SCPs (646, 871, 1680), create a constant stream of mass from nowhere. Is that a problem?
item.content:encoded: I am wondering if the Foundation has any plan for dealing with all the excess mass that results from these SCPs. They've found short-term ways to keep the Keter cakes from overrunning the planet, but the mass of the consumed cakes is still conserved by D-class digestion. The same goes for 646's terminated offspring and 1680's clones of Tyler Buchanan used as D-class. The mass of the SCP-verse's planet Earth is gradually increasing and, without some way to destroy all that mass or send it somewhere else, will continue to do so. Are there other anomalies that are constantly destroying mass and therefore balancing this somewhat? Or is the increase so small that it simply won't matter against the mass of the entire planet?

item.title: SCP Idea: Absolute Transfer Thermal Paste (Greenlight Wanted)
item.description: An SCP Idea, any and all feedback wanted.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a tube of Absolute TransferTM Thermal Paste. When applied to a single object, no effect is observed, however, when a second object is applied to the paste on the first object, all thermal energy from the second object is transferred into the first object, causing the second object to reach a temperature of 0 Kelvin, however only momentarily, as the object is heated up by air molecules hitting it. The first object gains the exact amount of thermal energy that was lost from the second object.

Central Narrative: This SCP was found during a raid on a member of Anderson Robotics (If that makes sense), and was confiscated and tested, as no trademark for "Absolute Transfer" Thermal Paste existed at the time.

Hook/Attention Grabber: This SCP has the ability to completely transfer all energy from one object to another.

Additional Notes: Does it make sense for the Foundation to raid the home of a member of Anderson Robotics, if not, are there any other GoIs that would make sense in this context?

item.title: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen
item.description: A sentient ink pen that wrote itself into existences--at least it thinks it did.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient ink pen with that experiences existential crisis. The God Pen looks like a regular high value ink pen from the 1930s. However when someone tries to write with it, they only thing they write is what the pen is thinking at the time. The person trying to write with it, thinks they are writing what they want to until they put the pen down. The pen's thoughts are mostly about it's own existence or experiences and it believes that it created its self.

Some experiences it has had include:

  • It's own painful creation out of nothing
  • Times of War
  • Being the Object of Warship by cults (hence the origin of it's name "The God Pen")
  • Being helpless to save someone, because it's basically just a pen

Super fast pitch: A self-aware intelligent ink pen meets Forrest Gump.

Central Narrative: A pen that can think and feel questioning it own existence and it's own uncertainties of it's life and possible death. Basically the fleeting and uncertainty of life as told by an ink pen that has gathered a number of life experiences over the decades.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A Ink pen that thinks it wrote itself into existences.

Additional Notes: Open to suggestions as I want to make this the best that it can be.
